summary: The note examines the labor shortage and talent gap facing small businesses as of October 2023, driven by the pandemic and fast-changing technology and consumer behavior. It cites an NFIB figure that about 49% of small businesses struggled to fill positions. It then profiles strategies from named business owners, including apprenticeships, broader recruitment, policy advocacy, culture and benefits, school partnerships, upskilling, remote work, and AI-based HR tools.
one_line: Small businesses in late 2023 face labor shortages and a skills gap, and are responding with training, apprenticeships, remote work, partnerships, and HR technology.
key_facts: A National Federation of Independent Business report indicated approximately 49% of small businesses struggled with filling job positions in the first quarter post-September 2023, a statistic that has been steadily climbing.
Anna Rodriguez runs a boutique digital marketing firm in San Francisco, where labor scarcity has caused delayed projects and overburdened staff.
Rodriguez said on October 15, 2023 that there is a mismatch between job-seekers' skills and the skills her firm needs.

Michael Chen, CEO of SecureTech, a small data protection firm, said on November 12, 2023 that many cybersecurity programs do not equip students with applied skills for immediate operational competence.
Kelly Thompson, who leads a specialty welding company in Houston, started an apprenticeship program in early September 2023 where apprentices earn while they learn and pick up certifications.

Stephanie Cruz, HR manager at a renewable energy startup, said in a September 26, 2023 webinar that her company broadened its search beyond job boards to specialized schools, community programs, and social media.

Amar Singh, a restaurateur, is part of a coalition advocating immigration reform to ease work visa restrictions, and said on October 8, 2023 that quicker hiring of skilled immigrants could be a game-changer for hospitality.
Clara Bennett, owner of a biotech research company in Raleigh, says her company competes through culture: flexible schedules, continuous learning, and an inclusive environment.
James Kim, co-founder of an electronics repair service, partners with a local tech school to cultivate the specific skills his industry requires.
Rachel Warner, who manages a graphic design studio in Portland, has set aside a budget specifically for ongoing training, workshops, and certifications.
Laura Ortiz, a SaaS entrepreneur, says remote positions expand the search beyond geographical constraints.
Tom Nguyen, who runs an IT services company in Austin, integrated AI-based analysis into recruitment, improving applicant quality and substantially reducing time to hire.
The note concludes that there is no single silver bullet for labor shortages and that a multifaceted, proactive approach is needed.
